summary: Virginia Tech, Amazon and independent authors propose Belief-Calibrated Optimization (BCO). When a coding agent iteratively edits an agent scaffold around a frozen model, BCO keeps a persistent 'world model' document of beliefs about how the environment responds to edits. Before each candidate it writes a prediction, then grades and corrects that prediction against observed outcomes. Against a matched vanilla optimization loop on five benchmarks (LongMemEval-s, LoCoMo, GAIA, AppWorld, Terminal-Bench 2.0), BCO's selected candidate scores higher on train and held-out. Mixed target-model-swap results and an offline prediction ablation are also reported.

claims.claim: BCO reaches higher train and held-out passrate than a matched control lacking only the world model, on all five benchmarks.
claims.evidence: Table 1 held-out: LME 0.533->0.608, LoCoMo 0.375->0.453, GAIA 0.343->0.495, AppWorld 0.766->0.796, TB2.0 0.470->0.492. But each comparison is one trajectory per method (§7). In the 3-trajectory LME diagnostic (Table 3) within-method ranges are 0.11-0.13, larger than the small gaps on TB2.0 (+0.022 on 66 tasks) and AppWorld (+0.030). Consistent direction across 5 benchmarks is the real evidence.

claims.claim: After a target-model swap the BCO scaffold leads, except where context overruns leave it unfinished.
claims.evidence: GAIA: BCO highest at all three gpt-5.6-luna effort tiers. AppWorld full set: BCO 0.516/0.524/0.532 vs vanilla 0.685/0.608/0.538, so BCO is worst at high and medium effort because its unbounded scratchpad caused 99/77/65 of 372 tasks to return no output. The abstract's framing downplays a real failure.

claims.claim: The world-model document carries reusable predictive information in its content, not just its form.
claims.evidence: Table 2 (40 candidates): upside hit rate None 0.441 < Scrambled 0.460 < Intact 0.538; downside precision 0.142 < 0.181 < 0.217; LLM judges (Kimi-K2.6/DeepSeek-V4-Flash) agree. With runs as the independent unit (4 runs), the two-sided sign test gives p=0.125, which the authors report, so this is not significant.

claims.claim: Persistence alone (free-form notes) does not reproduce BCO's gain.
claims.evidence: Table 3 LME, 3 trajectories: vanilla 0.430, Notes 0.427, BCO 0.467, with ranges 0.11/0.07/0.13. The authors concede three short runs cannot show notes are ineffective.

patterns.note: Agent-driven scaffold search improved by an explicit, calibrated belief document; consistent but small and single-trajectory gains.
A structured, calibrated persistent document helps more than free-form notes in one small diagnostic. An unbounded scratchpad re-injected every turn broke transfer on AppWorld.
Negative evidence for no compaction: BCO's unbounded scratchpad caused context overruns, while vanilla's 16-exchange sliding window completed every task.
AppWorld scaffold is a ReAct code-as-action agent; not the object of study.
LLM judges used for the pairwise prediction comparison, cross-checked by judge-free metrics.

methodology.sample: 5 benchmarks with train/test splits: LME 100/400, LoCoMo 80/1449, GAIA 40/99, AppWorld 45/372 (scenario-disjoint), TB2.0 20/66; 40 candidates in the offline ablation; 3 trajectories per method in the LME persistence diagnostic.
methodology.baselines: A matched vanilla iterative optimization loop (same proposer, target, initial scaffold, budget). No comparison to published optimizers (e.g., ADAS/DSPy/GEPA-style) in the main table.
methodology.models: Targets DeepSeek-V4-Flash and MiniMax-M3; proposers Kimi-K2.6, Kimi-K2.7, GPT-5.6 via Codex; swap target gpt-5.6-luna.
methodology.variance: One trajectory per method per benchmark; temperature 0, one repeat per task (k=2 on TB2.0). Variance is shown only in the 3-run LME diagnostic; sign test p=0.125 for the offline ablation.
methodology.ablations: Scrambled vs intact vs no document (offline); Notes-only persistence (LME).
methodology.contamination_controls: Held-out splits not used for selection; AppWorld split scenario-disjoint. The train subsets for AppWorld/TB2.0 were stability-screened after inspecting initial-scaffold behaviour (acknowledged).
methodology.languages: Python scaffolds; agent tasks are QA, app APIs and shell, not code generation in Java.

standards.artifacts: No code repository linked in text or metadata; the protocol and an example prediction are given verbatim in Appendix B.

biases.detail: Single trajectory per method on every main benchmark; the one variance check shows run-to-run spread exceeding several of the gaps.
Authors' own method against their own vanilla control; no external optimizer baselines.
Train subsets screened to remove oscillating tasks after seeing initial behaviour; the authors note this may favour benchmarks where score-guided optimization is easier.
The abstract's 'leads on the tasks we test, except where context-window overruns' hides that BCO is last on AppWorld's full set at two of three tiers.

coi.affiliations: Virginia Tech, Amazon, and an independent researcher (per-author mapping not recoverable from the parsed text).
coi.vendor_products_evaluated: No Amazon product evaluated; third-party open-weight targets and proposers (DeepSeek, MiniMax, Kimi, OpenAI).
coi.funding: No acknowledgments or funding section found.
coi.detail: Partial vendor affiliation without self-promotion of a product.

verdict_reason: A careful matched design with held-out splits, five benchmarks and an unusually candid limitations section. But each comparison is a single trajectory with gaps comparable to the measured run-to-run spread, the content ablation is non-significant (p=0.125), the transfer result is mixed, and no code is released.
applicability: Indirect. For a team tuning its own harness (prompts, AGENTS.md/system specs, retrieval over the ≥4 ingestion repos), the useful idea is procedural. When an agent proposes a harness change, require a written prediction ('this edit should fix failure class X and not regress Y') and grade it against eval results in a committed belief/decision log. That keeps the LLM-proposes, deterministic-check-decides split and stays host-independent because it is just a file in git. Two warnings transfer directly. Bound any persistent scratchpad: an unbounded one broke on a more verbose model, which matters when hosts route to different models. And re-validate a tuned scaffold whenever the host's model changes. No Java, code-generation or healthcare-content evidence.

conflicts_with.detail: That paper shows self-authored verification is unreliable in self-improving agents. BCO's belief self-grading is also self-authored, though the final selection uses the benchmark's fixed external graders and held-out splits.
